tagline: The old toll road around Grandfather, from before the Parkway.
intro: From Linville, laid out in 1883 by a Kansan named Samuel T. Kelsey, US 221 swings around the flank of Grandfather Mountain on its way to Blowing Rock. Along the way, signs mark the Eastern Continental Divide, the invisible line between water bound for the Atlantic and water bound for the Gulf of Mexico.

Men and mules cut the road in 1889 as a private toll road, the Yonahlossee Trail. It was the link between Linville and Blowing Rock until the Blue Ridge Parkway, which runs along the same mountain, was finally completed in 1987.

moments.title: Linn Cove Viaduct
moments.text: Across the face of Grandfather the Parkway's last link curls around the rock on a concrete viaduct, set segment by segment from above so no heavy equipment touched the mountainside.

moments.title: Westglow
moments.text: The columned Colonial Revival house near Blowing Rock was painter Elliott Daingerfield's summer home, and his "Madonna of the Hills" hangs in town at St. Mary's-of-the-Hills Episcopal Church.

moments.title: Blowing Rock
moments.text: The town takes its name from a cliff over the Johns River Valley, where the air comes up so strongly that light things tossed off it are blown back.

practical: The route is not recommended for recreational vehicles or buses.
